In reinforcement learning, experience replay is a crucial technique for improving the efficiency of training. This results in the replay buffer containing outdated experiences that are not relevant to the current policy, leading to suboptimal performance. To address this issue, we propose a new experience replay algorithm that dynamically adjusts the replay buffer based on the variance of the experiences. This algorithm, called Variance Decrease based Experience Replay (VDER), is designed to maintain a diverse replay buffer that is relevant to the current policy. We demonstrate the effectiveness of VDER in various reinforcement learning tasks, including Atari games and MuJoCo environments. The results show that VDER outperforms the standard experience replay algorithm in terms of sample efficiency and performance. Additionally, we provide a theoretical analysis of VDER and show that it can be viewed as a variant of the importance sampling algorithm. This analysis provides a deeper understanding of the behavior of VDER and its relationship to importance sampling. We also provide a practical implementation of VDER that is easy to use and integrate into existing reinforcement learning algorithms.
